notes: Watford does not run selective licensing or additional HMO licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies: you need a licence if your property is let to five or more people forming two or more households. New applications cost £1,557.70.
research: PRIMARY: the 'Licensable HMOs' page (also served at /hmolicensing) states verbatim: 'Houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) require a licence if they are occupied by: five or more people from two or more households... A licence lasts up to five years.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED, mandatory-only: a single fee ladder with no occupancy or area banding and no separate cost-recovery route: 'New Application Fee - £1,557.70 / New Application Fee Registered Charities - £1,236.90 / Renewal Fee - £1,295.90 / Renewal Fee Registered Charities - £1,033 / Assisted HMO licence application - £362.30 / Fast track licence application - £403.70.' There is no selective-licensing fee line and no second application route. SCOPE TEST: the council's Licensing index lists its full licence catalogue, 'Taxi and private hire, Entertainment and alcohol, Gambling, Landlord licences, Piercing and cosmetic procedure, Animal, Special event', and the 'Landlord licences' entry links to the HMO page, i.e. mandatory HMO licensing is the ONLY property licence Watford issues. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 200 (56,696 bytes) and was fully enumerated; zero URLs contain 'selectiv'; the only 'additional' hit is a food-waste news article, excluded. All five HMO sub-pages and the standards-in-rented-properties page were fetched and grepped in RAW HTML for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen': zero hits. TRAPS EXCLUDED: no Article 4 direction was mistaken for licensing; the Renters' Rights Act 2025 download was not read as Housing Act 2004 s.56 (the RRA s.56 rent-bidding trap); the s.254 three-person definition was not treated as a licensing threshold. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing from Three Rivers was carried across; only watford.gov.uk pages were used. LIMITATION: Watford's site search is Cludo (JavaScript); the Cludo v3 API returned '{"Message":"An error has occurred."}' for the positive control, the real query and the nonsense control alike, so the site search proved nothing and was disregarded. The finding rests on the primary page text, the fee schedule, the licence catalogue and the complete sitemap sweep, which agree.

notes: Waverley runs mandatory HMO licensing only. The council states no other licensing schemes are in operation or being proposed. You need a licence if you let to five or more people forming two or more households. New applications cost £807.70, renewals £710.50.
research: STRONGEST EVIDENCE IN THE BATCH, an explicit and unusually complete council denial, confirmed in RAW HTML rather than rendered text: 'Waverley operates a mandatory HMO licensing scheme that covers the entire Borough, no other licensing schemes are in operation or are being proposed. There are no Article 4 HMO Direction and Short-Term Let Schemes or Restrictions in force and under consideration.' That single sentence rules out BOTH Part 3 selective licensing and Part 2 s.56 additional licensing, disposes of any 'proposed' status, and pre-emptively rules out the Article 4 trap that has caught eight of the last twelve councils. THRESHOLD: 'you rent your property to five or more people who form more than one household [and] tenants share toilet, bathroom or kitchen facilities.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED: fees are held as HTML entities, so the raw-HTML grep was rerun for the pound entity; the complete set recovered is £807.70 (new applications, per property), £710.50 (renewal after five years), £30.60 (surcharge for 11-15 units), £12.20 (per unit above 15), £25 (approved landlords association discount) and £100 (late application fee). The ladder starts at five occupants and every extra charge is a per-unit surcharge on a mandatory licence. The £30.60 and £12.20 lines were correctly excluded as the 'additional fee / per unit' trap rather than read as additional licensing. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 200 (185,936 bytes) and was fully enumerated; zero URLs contain 'selectiv'; the single 'Additional' hit is a planning application title ('Amended Additional Information'), excluded. A raw-HTML grep of the 156,932-byte HMO page for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits beyond the denial quoted above.

notes: Wealden states it does not operate a selective licensing scheme and has no plans to do so. There is no additional HMO licensing either. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for five or more people in two or more households. Fees start at £808 for a five-person shared house.
research: EXPLICIT DENIAL found by RAW-HTML grep, under its own h2 heading on the council's HMO page: 'Selective Licensing - Wealden District Council does not currently operate a selective licensing scheme and has no plans to do so.' A direct primary-source negative for Part 3 that also disposes of any 'proposed' status. ADDITIONAL LICENSING: no s.56 scheme. The page's licensing trigger is 'Which HMOs must be licensed? It is now compulsory from the 1st October 2018 to licence all HMOs that: Have five or more people from two or more households (i.e. people not related, living together as a couple, etc); and Share amenities', the 2018 mandatory extension, and the page elsewhere describes 'the revised mandatory scheme'. A raw-HTML grep for 'additional licen' returned zero hits. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED: 'Initial Fee For a standard 5 person shared house - £808 / 6 persons - £823 / 7 persons - £839 / 8 persons - £855 / 9 persons - £870 (each person thereafter incurs an additional cost of £16)'. The shared-house ladder STARTS AT FIVE OCCUPANTS, the strong mandatory-only signal. A second band exists for bedsit-type HMOs ('2 individual bedsit units - £933... 6 units - £1184, each unit thereafter £63'); this starts at two UNITS, not two occupants, and was checked not to imply additional licensing: it is a fee band for converted and bedsit HMOs that must still cross the stated five-person occupancy trigger to be licensable. The £16 and £63 lines were excluded as the per-additional-unit surcharge trap. SITEMAP: /sitemap.xml 301s, but /wp-sitemap.xml returned HTTP 200 and its posts-page sub-file (193,267 bytes) was fully enumerated; zero 'selectiv' URLs. The mandatory-conditions boilerplate on the page ('There are mandatory conditions which require the licence holder to: Produce an annual gas safety certificate...') was correctly read as licence conditions, not as evidence of a discretionary scheme.

notes: Welwyn Hatfield does not run selective licensing or additional HMO licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, to properties let to five or more people. The council's published fee schedule starts at a basic five-person HMO, costing £1,339 in 2026/27.
research: PRIMARY PAGE: 'Apply for a House of Multiple Occupation Licence' states 'If you are renting out a House of Multiple Occupation (HMO) which has five or more unrelated people occupying it you will need to apply for a licence.' All five sub-pages and the landlords hub were fetched and grepped in RAW HTML for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen': zero hits. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED, AND THIS IS THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE. The web page defers fees to a document, so the council's 31-page General Fund Fees and Charges 2026-27 PDF (11.2MB) was downloaded and its full text extracted. The HMO section reads: 'HMO Application - Application for basic 5 person HMO* / Application for an HMO between 6 - 10 persons* / Application for an HMO with 11 or more persons* / *10% discount on HMO fee for member of PAL scheme', with amounts £1,290.00 / £1,443.00 / £1,589.00 rising to £1,339.00 / £1,498.00 / £1,650.00 for 2026-27. The ladder STARTS AT FIVE PERSONS, and critically, a full-text search of the entire 31-page statutory fee schedule for 'selective licen', 'additional licen', 'part 3' and 'section 56' produced NO cost-recovery line for any discretionary scheme. A live scheme must be self-financing, so its absence from the council's own statutory fee schedule is close to conclusive. TRAPS EXCLUDED: the one 'additional' hit in the PDF ('Combination of activities equal to highest fee plus 50% of each additional licensable activity') is Licensing Act 2003 alcohol and entertainment boilerplate, not s.56. The Renters' Rights Act pages were checked and not confused with Housing Act 2004 s.56. The 'PAL scheme' discount is voluntary landlord accreditation, excluded. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml HTTP 200 (24,441 bytes), fully enumerated, zero 'selectiv' URLs; the 'additional' hits are a benefits page and two local-plan documents, excluded.

notes: West Berkshire does not run selective licensing or additional HMO licensing. Its housing licensing is delivered by the Public Protection Partnership, which states mandatory licensing applies to HMOs occupied by five or more people forming two or more households.
research: DELEGATION NOTE, IMPORTANT FOR SOURCING: West Berkshire delivers its housing regulation through the Public Protection Partnership (PPP), its statutory shared regulatory service with Bracknell Forest. Both council URLs 301-redirect there, verified with curl -I: /houses-multiple-occupation redirects to publicprotectionpartnership.org.uk/houses-in-multiple-occupation-hmo, and /article/40653/Rented-housing-standards-and-licensing redirects to publicprotectionpartnership.org.uk/housing. PPP is therefore the council's own service under delegation, not a third-party aggregator; the westberks.gov.uk URL is cited because the redirect makes it authoritative, and no landlord blog, letting agent or aggregator was relied on. PRIMARY TEXT, recovered by grepping the RAW HTML because the content sits below a large navigation block and is easy to miss in rendered text: 'What is a licensable HMO? The licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Prescribed Description) (England) Order 2018, came into effect on 1 October 2018 which extends the current mandatory licensing scheme across England. Mandatory licensing applies to HMOs that are occupied by five or more occupants which form two households or more and meeting the "standard tests" (Section 254(2)...).' The scheme is described purely as mandatory. A raw-HTML grep of the page for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits. TRAP EXCLUDED: the page cites s.254(2), which is the DEFINITION of an HMO and not a licensing threshold, and was not read as evidence of a three-person discretionary scheme. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml HTTP 200 (60,490 bytes), fully enumerated; only two housing-licensing URLs exist in the entire sitemap, both redirecting to PPP as above, and zero URLs contain 'selectiv'. LIMITATION: WebFetch on the PPP host returned HTTP 403; this was worked around with curl using a browser user-agent plus Accept, Accept-Language, Referer and --compressed, which returned HTTP 200, so the 403 was a bot block and not evidence. PPP's HMO fee lines could not be extracted because they sit on a separate fees-and-charges route, so THE FEE-SCHEDULE TEST IS UNAPPLIED HERE; the negative rests on the explicit 'mandatory licensing' wording plus the sitemap sweep. This is the weakest-sourced record in the batch.

notes: West Devon does not run selective licensing or additional HMO licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies: a licence is needed if the property is let to five or more people forming two or more households. The licence fee is £446.40, plus a £144 fit and proper person fee.
research: PRIMARY: the dedicated 'HMO licensing' page states 'HMOs must be licensed by the council if the property is let to five or more people who form two or more households', repeated verbatim as the summary on the parent HMO page. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED: 'The HMO Licence fee is £446.40. The licence needs to be renewed every five years. The Fit and Proper fee is £144.00.' A SINGLE flat licence fee with no banding, no area-specific route and no second application form; there is no separate cost-recovery fee for any discretionary scheme, which a live scheme would be legally required to carry. The only application routes offered are the West Devon HMO application and renewal forms, both emailed to the shared South West Devon licensing address; no selective or additional route exists. A raw-HTML grep of both HMO pages for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml HTTP 200 (36,518 bytes), fully enumerated; the complete HMO tree (about-hmos, hmo-fact-sheet and its appeals, exemptions, fit-and-proper-person, HHSRS and management-orders sub-pages) is present and contains no selective or additional licensing page; zero URLs contain 'selectiv'; the two 'additional' hits are a land-charges searches page and a tree-works page, both excluded. TRAP EXCLUDED: the site has a 'Landlords and SeaMoor Lettings' section. SeaMoor Lettings is the council's own lettings agency, a landlord and tenant matching service, and was correctly NOT read as a 'selective lettings' or property-licensing scheme. LIMITATION: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on this host; retrying with curl plus a browser user-agent and full headers returned HTTP 200, so the 403 was a bot block, not evidence. The page is Drupal-rendered with a very large inline cookie-consent JSON blob, so the body was extracted by stripping tags rather than trusting a rendered summary.

notes: West Lancashire does not run selective licensing or additional HMO licensing, including in Skelmersdale. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies: a licence is needed if the property is occupied by five or more people forming two or more households.
research: CHECKED WITH EXTRA CARE given Skelmersdale's large private rented sector. PRIMARY: the 'Houses in multiple occupation' page, footer-stamped 'Last Updated | Thursday, May 7, 2026 | 4:40 PM' and therefore current, states: 'Does a HMO have to be licensed? A HMO must be licensed if the property is occupied by five or more people forming two or more households. For example, a property being rented by 5 single people who are not related to each other will need a licence.' The only application route offered is the national portal: 'You can apply for a new HMO licence or renew an existing licence online through the gov.uk portal.' No area-specific or street-specific route exists anywhere on the site. SITE SEARCH, CONTROLS RUN AND PASSED, so a nil result here genuinely means something. The search endpoint was found by reading the homepage form (action=/searchresults.aspx, name='search'; note /search-results.aspx 404s and several parameter names silently return an empty shell). POSITIVE CONTROL 'council tax' returned '1283 results'. NEGATIVE CONTROL 'zzqxwvplopfoo' returned zero results with a distinct 13,093-byte response. Real queries returned distinct byte sizes, distinct MD5s and distinct counts ('houses in multiple occupation' 487, 'additional licensing' 317, 'selective licensing' 159), proving the engine discriminates rather than echoing a fixed page. The 'selective licensing' results were then READ: every hit is an OR-match on the word 'licensing' alone (Licensing, Licensing policy, Contact the licensing team, Taxi Licensing Policy, Licensed premises complaints, Licensing Act 2003, gaming machine permits, TENs). NOT ONE concerns Part 3 or s.56. SITEMAP LIMITATION, STATED HONESTLY: robots.txt advertises /sitemap.aspx, but both /sitemap and /sitemap.aspx return a broken stub, literally 'Error parsing XSLT file: CultivSearchEngineSitemap.xslt' inside an empty urlset, so the sitemap sweep was UNAVAILABLE. This was compensated by crawling the housing and private-housing pages and enumerating every child (empty-homes, grants-and-schemes, help-advice-for-private-sector-tenants, leaseholders, mobile-homes-fit-proper-person-test, house-condition-surveys, private-sector-housing-strategy, private-sector-housing-enforcement), grepping each in RAW HTML for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen': zero hits, including in the enforcement page, which is where civil-penalty boilerplate would normally surface. TRAPS EXCLUDED: the page opens with the s.254 definition ('At least 3 tenants live there forming more than one household'), which defines an HMO and is NOT a licensing threshold; the threshold is separately and explicitly stated as five. The Mandatory Conditions of Licences Regulations 2018 discussion is licence conditions, not a scheme. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing was carried over from Liverpool, Sefton or Blackpool.

notes: West Oxfordshire does not run selective licensing or additional HMO licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, to properties occupied by five or more people forming two or more households. Fees are £242 to apply plus £1,097 to issue a new licence.
research: PRIMARY: the 'Houses in multiple occupation' page requires a licence where a property is 'occupied by five or more people, forming two or more households' and where 'tenants share facilities such as kitchen or bathrooms'; licences are 'valid for five years'. A raw-HTML grep for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED: a two-part fee, 'Application Fee (Part 1) £242.00' plus 'New Licence Issue Fee (Part 2) £1,097.00', with an 'Additional room fee (7+ rooms) £41.00 per room'; renewals £242.00 plus £994.00 with a 7+ rooms surcharge of £21.00 per room capped at £200.00. One scheme, one route, no discretionary cost-recovery line. The 'additional room fee' was correctly excluded as the per-room surcharge trap. SITE SEARCH, CONTROLS RUN AND PASSED. The endpoint was found from the homepage form (action=/Search/, name='query'). POSITIVE CONTROL 'council tax' returned '342 results'. NEGATIVE CONTROL 'zzqxwvplopfoo' returned 'No results' with a distinct 4,402-byte response, so the engine can return zero and a nil result is meaningful. 'selective licensing' returned 59 results, but these were READ rather than trusted: every result is an OR-match on 'licensing' alone (business-and-licensing, alcohol-and-entertainment, club premises certificates, personal licence, premises licence, animal, primate and zoo licences, plus unrelated corporate pages). Quoting the phrase returned the identical 59, confirming the engine ignores phrase operators and does OR matching, so the count is noise rather than a positive. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml 404s but the bare /sitemap returns HTTP 200 (21,512 bytes), the fallback that has worked for Wakefield, Torbay, Rushmoor and Teignbridge, and was fully enumerated; zero 'selectiv' URLs; the whole private-housing tree is present with no selective or additional page. TRAPS EXCLUDED, ONE NOTABLE: the sitemap contains an ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION at /planning-and-building/article-4-directions/article-4/multiple-sites-2016/, the commonest error in this dataset. It is planning control over C3-to-C4 conversion, creates no licence requirement, and was excluded. Also excluded: the civil-penalties-and-charges page, which is the boilerplate that routinely cites 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [s95 Housing Act 2004]' without any scheme existing.

notes: Westmorland and Furness does not run selective or additional HMO licensing, and inherited no scheme from Barrow-in-Furness, Eden or South Lakeland. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for five or more people. The fee is £700 for a 5-bedroom property, £20 per room thereafter.
research: CHECKED WITH EXTRA CARE. This is a 2023 unitary formed from Barrow-in-Furness, Eden and South Lakeland, so a pre-vesting-day district designation could still have been running to about 2028. The retired predecessor domains were swept as was done for Somerset, and nothing was found. CURRENT COUNCIL, PRIMARY: 'If your HMO is rented to five or more people, forming at least two households, it needs a licence. Each licensable HMO will need its own licence.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED, verified in RAW HTML: 'A license fee currently costs £700 for a 5-bedroom property, £20 per room thereafter for both new licenses and renewals. A HMO licence can last for up to five years.' The ladder STARTS AT FIVE BEDROOMS, the strong mandatory-only signal, and the '£20 per room thereafter' line was excluded as the per-room surcharge trap. Raw-HTML greps of the HMO licence page, the HMO standards page, the housing-standards index and the advice-for-landlords page for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is a Drupal index; both sub-files were fetched (447,280 and 282,180 bytes) and fully enumerated. Zero URLs contain 'selectiv'. The complete housing-standards tree is visible and contains only advice-about-empty-properties, advice-landlords, advice-property-managers-and-letting-agents, advice-tenants, damp-mould-and-cold, houses-multiple-occupation-hmos, how-we-assess-property, immigration-inspection, renters-rights-act-2025 and report-empty-property; no licensing designation page. PREDECESSOR SWEEP via the Wayback CDX API, the decisive check: barrowbc.gov.uk returned 24,611 distinct archived URLs with ZERO containing 'selectiv'; eden.gov.uk and southlakeland.gov.uk were swept the same way with zero 'selectiv' hits. The CONTENT of Barrow's final pre-vesting-day HMO page was then read (snapshot 20230607144916, i.e. weeks after the 1 April 2023 vesting day and already footer-stamped 'Westmorland and Furness Council 2023'). It is headed 'Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation - Mandatory Licensing' and says: 'From 3rd July 2006 all liable HMO landlords must licence their properties, however, not all HMOs will require a licence under the mandatory scheme... it is still 5 or more people in 2 or more households and sharing amenities, however, the 3 storey rule has gone.' Its only application route is 'this Mandatory Licensing Scheme Application Form'. Barrow, the district most likely to have designated given its terraced stock, was running mandatory licensing ONLY at the point of abolition, so nothing could have carried forward to 2028. TRAP EXCLUDED: the planning advice page on HMO conversion is PLANNING advice, not licensing, and was not counted. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing was carried over from Lancaster. LIMITATION, STATED HONESTLY: the council's site search FAILED ITS POSITIVE CONTROL and proves nothing. The correct endpoint is /search?keys= (found by reading the homepage form; the first attempt at /search?search_api_fulltext= was wrong), but results are injected by JavaScript: the positive control 'council tax' returned the same ~11.8KB shell with no visible results as the nonsense control, so the search was disregarded entirely. The ModernGov instance is live (HTTP 200) but /mgSearch.aspx 404s and returned a byte-identical page for the positive control, the real query and the nonsense control, so committee-paper search was also unavailable. The negative rests on the primary page text, the fee ladder, the complete two-part sitemap sweep and the three predecessor-domain archive sweeps, which all agree.
